## Epic Details

### E1: Factory Overview + Shared Foundation

**Priority tier:** Must (MVP)
**Dependencies:** None — can start immediately
**Value delivered:** An operator landing on `/` can immediately see whether the factory is connected, how big it is, how many problems are unacknowledged, and jump straight to them. This epic also lays the shared groundwork (status color maps, alert normalization, the missing "all machines" hook) that every later epic reuses.

**User Stories:**

| ID | Story | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------|----------|---------------------|
| US-001 | As an operator, I want to see connection status, machine count, zone count, and uptime on landing so that I know the system is live and how big the floor is (S1) | Must | - 4 `StatTile`s render from `useFactoryStatus`<br>- Skeleton while loading, error message on failure |
| US-002 | As an operator, I want to see how many unacknowledged critical/warning alerts exist, with a link to them, so that I know where to focus right away (S2) | Must | - Attention banner shows correct counts<br>- Links to `/alerts`<br>- Shows "All clear" when zero |

**Functional Requirements Included:**

| Req ID | Description | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| FR-001 | Overview KPI row | Must |
| FR-002 | Machine status breakdown via `useAllMachines` | Should |
| FR-003 | Attention banner | Must |
| FR-004 | Loading/error/empty states (dashboard portion) | Must |
| FR-010 | Alert normalization layer | Must |

**Build notes:** Create `src/lib/status.ts` (color maps), `src/lib/alerts.ts` (`normalizeAlert`, `sortAlerts`, safe timestamp handling), `src/hooks/useAllMachines.ts` (`useQueries` fanned across `useZones()` results, hitting `/api/zones/:zoneId/machines`), `src/components/StatTile.tsx` (modeled on `SampleCard.tsx`), `src/components/AttentionBanner.tsx`. Wire into `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`. Git init + push the starter to a new public GitHub repo before writing code; commit again when this epic is done.

**Definition of Done for this Epic:**
- [ ] `npm run dev` shows `/` with 4 correct KPI values and no console errors
- [ ] Attention banner shows "2 critical · 2 warning unacknowledged" against the default mock data and links to `/alerts`
- [ ] Skeletons appear on first load
- [ ] A user can land on the Dashboard and state the factory's connection status and open-problem count within 5 seconds

---

### E2: Active Problems (built for high alert volume)

**Priority tier:** Must (MVP)
**Dependencies:** E1 (requires `src/lib/status.ts`, `src/lib/alerts.ts`)
**Value delivered:** An operator can see every active problem, understand it at a glance, filter to what matters, and acknowledge it — and this holds up whether there are 6 alerts (today) or 50+ (a bad day), per product's explicit volume guidance.

**User Stories:**

| ID | Story | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------|----------|---------------------|
| US-003 | As an operator, I want a list of active alerts (severity, machine, zone, message, age), most urgent first (S3) | Must | - All fields render correctly, including the 3 known bad records (`alt-004/005/006`) |
| US-004 | As an operator, I want to filter by severity and zone (S4) | Must | - Filters combine; `?zone=` URL param supported |
| US-005 | As an operator, I want to acknowledge an alert (S5) | Must | - Pending state → toast → row updates |
| US-011 | As an operator on a bad day (50+ alerts), I want grouping by machine, clickable severity counts, and bulk acknowledge (S11) | Must | - Stress scenario (50 alerts) collapses to 14 groups; chips read 10/21/19; bulk-ack works on a group |

**Functional Requirements Included:**

| Req ID | Description | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| FR-004 | Loading/error/empty states (alerts portion) | Must |
| FR-005 | Alert list rendering | Must |
| FR-006 | Default sort | Must |
| FR-007 | Severity + zone filters | Must |
| FR-008 | Acknowledge action | Must |
| FR-009 | Show/hide acknowledged toggle | Should |
| FR-019 | Severity summary chips | Must |
| FR-020 | Group by machine (default) with flat toggle | Must |
| FR-021 | Bulk acknowledge | Should |
| FR-022 | Collapsed info-alert section | Should |
| FR-024 | Text search | Could |

**Build notes:** Build in this order to keep something demoable at every step: (1) `useActiveAlerts` (REST-only for now — live merge arrives in E4) + flat `AlertsTable` + single-row acknowledge; (2) severity chips (FR-019); (3) machine grouping as the default view with a flat-view toggle (FR-020); (4) bulk acknowledge per group and "acknowledge all shown" (FR-021); (5) collapse info alerts (FR-022); (6) search, only if time remains (FR-024). Use `window.__setAlertScenario("stress")` continuously while building steps 2–4 to validate against 50 alerts, not just the default 6.

**Definition of Done for this Epic:**
- [ ] Filtering to severity=critical and zone=welding, then acknowledging `welder-02`'s alert, shows a success toast and the row updates
- [ ] `__setAlertScenario("empty")` shows a clear empty state with no errors
- [ ] `__setAlertScenario("stress")` shows 14 machine groups (not 50 flat rows) with chips reading Critical 10 · Warning 21 · Info 19; bulk-acknowledging a group works
- [ ] `alt-004` shows a real machine name (not "undefined"); `alt-005` shows "Unknown time" and sorts last; `alt-006` shows the correct zone name
- [ ] A user can identify and act on the most urgent problem within 5 seconds, at both 6 and 50 alerts

### E3: Zone Health

**Priority tier:** Must (MVP)
**Dependencies:** E1 (requires `src/lib/status.ts`)
**Value delivered:** A supervisor can see which zone needs attention first and jump straight into that zone's problems.

**User Stories:**

| ID | Story | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------|----------|---------------------|
| US-006 | As a supervisor, I want each zone's health, machine count, and open-alert counts, ranked by need for attention (S6) | Must | - 4 zone cards, sorted faulted > degraded > healthy |
| US-009 | As a supervisor, I want to click a zone and see its alerts (S9) | Should | - Navigates to `/alerts?zone={id}` pre-filtered |

**Functional Requirements Included:**

| Req ID | Description | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| FR-011 | Zone health cards | Must |
| FR-012 | Zone card click → filtered alerts | Should |

**Build notes:** `src/components/ZoneHealthCard.tsx`, added to `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` below the KPI row. Reuses the normalized/merged alert list from E2's `useActiveAlerts()` (called once, unfiltered, grouped by `zoneId` with `useMemo`) — avoids an N+1 query per zone card.

**Definition of Done for this Epic:**
- [ ] Packaging (faulted, per mock data) appears before Assembly/Painting (healthy) in the grid
- [ ] Each card shows the correct machine count and open critical/warning count
- [ ] Clicking the Packaging card opens `/alerts` with the zone filter set to Packaging

### E4: Real-Time Awareness

**Priority tier:** Should
**Dependencies:** E2 (requires `useActiveAlerts` to merge live data into)
**Value delivered:** Operators don't need to manually refresh to catch new problems as they happen, and can trust that what they're seeing is current.

**User Stories:**

| ID | Story | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------|----------|---------------------|
| US-007 | As an operator, I want new alerts to appear on their own, with critical ones notifying me (S7) | Should | - Live alert appears without refresh; critical fires a toast |
| US-008 | As an operator, I want to see that telemetry is streaming (S8) | Should | - Live pulse + "last update Ns ago" ticker |

**Functional Requirements Included:**

| Req ID | Description | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| FR-013 | Live alert stream merged into the list | Should |
| FR-014 | Live telemetry indicator | Should |
| FR-023 | Stable row order during live updates ("N new alerts" pill) | Should |

**Build notes:** `src/live/LiveProvider.tsx` (single `useFactoryWebSocket` subscription for the whole app, mounted once in `App.tsx` inside `QueryClientProvider`), `src/hooks/useLive.ts`. Update `useActiveAlerts` to merge `liveAlerts` from the provider (functional `setState`, not the query cache — the acknowledge mutation's `invalidateQueries(["alerts"])` would otherwise silently drop them). Route `acknowledgeAlert(id)` to a local-only ack path for any `ws-alt-*` id (the REST endpoint 404s on these). `src/components/LiveIndicator.tsx` for the Dashboard.

**Definition of Done for this Epic:**
- [ ] Leaving `/alerts` open for up to ~45s produces a new alert row without a manual refresh
- [ ] A critical live alert fires a toast immediately
- [ ] Acknowledging a live (`ws-alt-*`) alert works and doesn't throw a 404
- [ ] The Dashboard's Live indicator visibly ticks ("Ns ago")

---

### E5: Factory Topology

**Priority tier:** Could
**Dependencies:** E1 (requires `useAllMachines`, `src/lib/status.ts`); E4 optional (for live tooltips)
**Value delivered:** A supervisor gets a physical mental map of the floor, seeing at a glance which machines in which zones are in trouble.

**User Stories:**

| ID | Story | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------|----------|---------------------|
| US-010 | As a supervisor, I want a visual floor layout of zones and machines colored by status, with live telemetry on hover (S10) | Could | - 4 zones, 14 machines, error machines stand out |

**Functional Requirements Included:**

| Req ID | Description | Priority |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| FR-015 | Topology zones + machine tiles by status | Could |
| FR-016 | Tile tooltip with live telemetry + flash on update | Could |

**Build notes:** `src/pages/Topology.tsx` only — a `SimpleGrid` of zone `Card`s, each containing a `Wrap` of machine tiles from `useAllMachines()`, colored via `machineStatusColor`. Tooltip pulls from `useLive().telemetry[machineId]` if E4 has landed; otherwise ship without live tooltips and note it as a cut.

**Definition of Done for this Epic:**
- [ ] All 4 zones and 14 machines render
- [ ] `welder-02` and `press-01` (both `status: "error"`) are visually distinct from running machines
- [ ] If E4 is done: hovering a machine shows its latest telemetry values
